methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.

original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one missing statement with quantified hypotheses, actual caller and existing coverage. A compact-switch lemma is a candidate only after its mathematical contract is reviewed. Establish a bounded proof plan before a separately budgeted proof-assistant build; do not rerun large Lean jobs as orientation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.

existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Kernel-check (Lean 4, Mathlib) a family of lower-bound and rung lemmas for P104 decoders, networks and words, on top of the earlier P104 Lean library carried unchanged: linear and Z/4-linear half-integer decoders (C >= 56 for Z/4-linear decoders), halving/doubling laws, the network potential and level-cut laws (NET8: D >= 56 with exactly 8 gathering and 8 depositing descents), future-attribution and carrier-run price bounds for class F/CF, Lemma T and the all-or-nothing law with the P104 frame data certified, the caller signed-Gram and relay-cut laws, and the port-general word rung at label rank h (molecule price, height-cut contract, word-shape lemma, budget certificates for h = 7 and 8). No kappa claim. Wall56 (and Wall56@Q96) is a premise wherever it is used. Not covered: hot intake outside class CF, the network-coding gain (NET-D56 core), denominators above 2 beyond the linear class, caller k > 71.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one uncovered interface implication; this package carries a family of theory lemmas (decoder, network, carrier-run, caller and rung statements), so the scope is wider than one implication. Recorded as changed.
bottleneck_link: Side result (theory and tooling). The lower-bound side of the P104 programme is mostly argued in notes; these statements are kernel-checked with their hypotheses stated, so a later proof of Wall56 (or a counterexample to it) can be plugged into a checked rung chain and the checked bounds can be reused instead of re-derived.
stop_rule: Ship only if every Check.lean declaration prints axioms within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorry/native_decide/axiom/extern appears in the sources, FrameCert.lean regenerates byte-identical, and verify.py passes; otherwise report the failing check.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, run in CI) checks sha256 pins of every stored file, token bans outside comments, module set, topological order and the All.lean closure, CHECK-axioms.txt against Check.lean (247 names, standard axioms only), toolchain and Mathlib pins, and regenerates FrameCert.lean byte-identical from data/frame. verify.sh additionally runs lean/check.sh (sequential guarded build of the 351-module closure and #print axioms of every Check.lean name).

open_questions.question: Can Wall56 (D >= 56 and R >= 56 per call, and its Q96 form) be proved?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every rung statement here takes the walls as a premise; the decoder and network lemmas cover the linear class, class F/CF runs and the 8-descent case only.
open_questions.first_step: Prove the NET-D56 core (D >= 56 for networks with arbitrary relay structure) or find a network below 56.
open_questions.blocked_by: The level-cut laws need D <= 55 to be used in their drop form; no proof or counterexample is known.
